newsitem.title: UK: SQUASH-JANSHER TO RETURN TO BRITISH SUPER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER TO RETURN TO BRITISH SUPER LEAGUE.

text.p: Pakistan world number one Jansher Khan has agreed to return to the British Super League less than 20 months after being accused of not trying in a match, a spokesman for the squash league said on Thursday.
Jansher, who will play for Surbiton in the 1996-97 campaign, missed the whole of last season while a disciplinary charge against him was settled.
The Pakistani, who is also world champion, was accused of not trying when losing to Scotland's Peter Nicol in March 1995. It was one of only two defeats suffered by Jansher in the past three years.
Playing for the Welsh Wizards, Jansher lost his match with current world number four Nicol, then playing for Cannons, 10-8 9-0 9-0, and it was the last two sets which sparked the lengthy dispute.
It was finally settled through arbitration after Jansher's argument of a dead rubber was accepted.
League director Andrew Shelley said: "It is all behind us. As long as Surbiton can find the funds to field him, he tells me he will be blowing his opponents away."
